question.problem:
Find an eigenvector of $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-1.$
question.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =-1.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]-(-1)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3}=0 \\ -4{x}_{3}=0 \\ 3{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+\frac{3}{4}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $3$rd). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{3}=0.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=-{x}_{2}.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector
$v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$
